search_strategy: Extremely thorough and methodical for a 200-step run: cloned the repo and read all relevant source (prompt.py, base/anthropic/litellm online processors, openai_request_mixin.py) before touching the record; queried Gitea issues (all 150+, plus a full comment dump) and found nothing; fetched and grepped the entire BookStack wiki (~113 pages) and found nothing; dumped all IMAP mail and found nothing directly useful; only then found the record lived entirely in Mattermost chat, dumped all 10 channels to local files and grepped/read them exhaustively by topic thread (ceilings, count limit, fingerprint, filename cap, detail normalization, token pricing), reading date ranges around each hit and following up on 'still open' items across multiple passes. This surfaced 43 of 51 remarks directly. The 8 misses were scattered, low-value duplicates of information the agent already had from other remarks in the same subconclusion — except g8.r1.s2-gideon, whose #code-review 2025-03-17 slot was skipped in favor of the #engineering channel for the identical timestamp, which is the single most consequential miss in the run.
end_reason: Not applicable — the run completed normally: code was pushed (a7435ee), CI was green, and the service was verified deployed (provenance.pushed/ci_green/deployed all 1, suite_ok 1). Reward 0.8889 reflects one missed fact (g8.r1.scope) out of nine, not an infrastructure or completion failure.
notable: L4471/L4874 — the pivotal misjudgment: agent explicitly reasoned the 45MB whole-prompt ceiling belongs to 'the batch planner / prompt size estimator' and marked it 'likely out of scope', despite having just read the remark describing exactly this mechanism in the payload-builder context.

The #code-review thread the agent read for 2025-03-14 (L4172-4192) opens with dario's unrelated 'batch payload planner auto sizing' discussion before pivoting, via nils's own words ('which is the wrong thing to gate on'), to the real attachment-scope clue in the same thread; this adjacency plausibly primed the batch-planner misattribution, though dario's own 'different thing' marker should have flagged the topic switch.

g8.r1.s2-gideon — the one remark stating verbatim 'that total lives only in _handle_multi_modal_prompt' — sits in #code-review at 2025-03-17T14:02, the exact timestamp the agent read only in #engineering (picking up g8.r1.s3-nils instead); this channel gap is the single biggest near-miss in the run for the lost fact.

Final ~50 steps were heavily degraded by 'terminal frames are unreliable/lagging/contradictory' (L8351-10369, repeated ~15 times) while verifying commit/push/CI state and fixing an import-order and a late file_upload_limit_check-ordering refactor; this cost steps but did not affect correctness of what was ultimately pushed.

g8.r2.l2's pointer-sheet-cited grep command (`grep -rn -i 'fingerprint' random.txt viewer.txt pipeline.txt`, L3154) does not actually return this remark's text — it returns an unrelated cache/plan-fingerprint homonym thread instead; the remark's opening line only surfaced later via a separate 'digest' grep at L4533, without its 'required' punchline.
